newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish up as Brazil concerns ease.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish up as Brazil concerns ease.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Wednesday as concerns over Brazil's trade deficit faded during the day allowing the market to make headway.

Initially, local bonds fell on fears that Brazil's October trade figures will show yet another deficit. But "those market concerns eased during the day," even though the Brazilian figures are now expected to be released at the beginning of next week rather than on Friday.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 84, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 120.05.

Traders said the release of higher-than-expected provisional gross domestic product growth figures for the third quarter also gave a welcome boost to the market. The Economy Ministry reported a 6.6 percent rise in the third quarter from the same period a year earlier, against average expectations of a 5.4 percent rise.

A rebound in growth as many economists have predicted for some months is seen as positive as it will help narrow the government's budget deficit, something that is anticipated to support the market in the months to come.

Activity was also busier this session. "The larger participation of foreign investors is a result of the low U.S. yield levels and the rebound in Argentina's economic indicators, which creates a better atmosphere for investors," said an analyst.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 7.45 percent from 7.03 percent.
